title: Continuation plan and acceptance criteria
summary: Complete the source-to-asset chain before making claims about multi-node execution or 500 GB bodycam footage. Existing 227 files are the practical first distributed workload.
invariants: First verify 83 legacy clips using independent ASR; do not regenerate blindly.
Next qualify local MediaPipe Tasks on real A02 footage with the Linux Foreign Runtime bridge.
Then bind pinned Storage Fabric references and Migratable Job checkpoint/placement semantics without a separate scheduler.
Only after two-node migration tests expand to 8–16 parallel workers and larger historical footage.
Keep person identification distinct from detection/tracking, and require independent identity policy and qualified evidence if identification is ever authorised.
procedure: Recover or regenerate useful readback assets; verify word timings and mouth PTS.
Test checkpoint/replay/migration and source hash enforcement on two real nodes.
Measure throughput, cost and failure recovery on 227 clips.
Scale to larger video subject to data-residency, authorization and evidence-retention controls.

provenance.claim: FFmpeg PTS range tracking and checkpoint interface, with MediaPipe not runtime-qualified.
83 source-pinned legacy recovery definitions and review-only candidate policy.
